messages:
Samir (CS): FYI customer reports being charged twice for the same streaming generation after an SSE disconnect. They say client reconnects and re-sends the prompt -> server returns a full completion twice. Repro attached. Need triage and billing hold :cry:

Jon (Support): dropping their repro here. short summary from customer: intermittent mobile network blips -> EventSource reconnect -> client posts same request without idempotency header. After reconnect they get a second final chunk that looks identical. They were billed for two full completions.

Samir (CS): customer repro (JS client):
```js
const es = new EventSource('/v1/streams?model=gpt-x');
es.onmessage = (e) => { /* append chunk */ }
es.onerror = () => { setTimeout(() => { // naive reconnect and re-request body 
  fetch('/v1/generate', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }) }) // this creates a new generation 
}, 2000) }
```

Marta (SRE): can you paste the server-side logs for the time window? need request ids / seq nums. If they just re-POSTed the generation on reconnect there's no idempotency on our API, so duplicates are expected unless resume semantics were used.

Samir (CS): pasted logs from the customer (redacted):
```
[2026-01-12T14:02:33Z] connection=conn-41 client_ip=1.2.3.4 session_token=sess-abc event: chunk seq=0 data="Hello"
[2026-01-12T14:02:41Z] connection=conn-41 network=timeout disconnect
[2026-01-12T14:02:44Z] incoming POST /v1/generate id=req-9001 body={"prompt":"..."} headers={}
[2026-01-12T14:02:45Z] start generation gen_id=gen-5a4f seq_start=0
[2026-01-12T14:02:46Z] completing generation gen_id=gen-5a4f final_token_count=312
```

Samir (CS): So on reconnect they did a POST instead of resuming. We did not reject because requests are allowed without idempotency. Result: two completed gens (the one from the original connection and the new one). Customer asked for refund.

Priya (Billing): please freeze billing for that customer while we investigate. If duplicates are confirmed we need to issue credit. Also, do we have a way to detect duplicate generations server-side?

Alex (Runtime): short answer: currently no global dedupe for non-idempotent POSTs. We do support resume tokens for streams (when client uses resume semantics). If the client had used the session resume token instead of re-POST we would have appended/continued rather than create a new generation.

Marta (SRE): adding more detail: our SSE resume flow uses a resume_token cookie that maps to a session and last_ack_seq. If client reconnects and sends a special query param `?resume_token=...` plus `last_ack=nn` we will attempt to resume and emit only outstanding chunks. Without that, POST will start new work.

Jon (Support): customer says mobile SDK didn't expose resume_token and their naive reconnection logic issues a fresh POST. They want guidance on client fix and a platform mitigation.

Samir (CS): proposed mitigation for customer: patch client to persist resume_token and send `?resume_token=...` on reconnect. Also include an `Idempotency-Key` header on creation requests so we can dedupe server-side. Example: `Idempotency-Key: cust-1234-prompta-20260112`

Alex (Runtime): Implementation notes for eng: server currently checks `Idempotency-Key` for sync endpoints and will dedupe if same key within 24h. However streaming endpoints create ephemeral streams tied to connections and we don't extract idempotency keys from the reconnection flow today. Could add logic: if incoming POST contains Idempotency-Key and we have a completed generation with same key within dedupe-window -> return 409 or the previous generation metadata instead of creating new work.

Marta (SRE): short-term mitigation we can enable: 1) Accept Idempotency-Key on POST/generate and check dedupe index. 2) On SSE side, ensure resume_token is returned in initial stream metadata payload so clients can persist. 3) Emit a metric when we detect same payload repeated from same session in a short window -> alert.

Samir (CS): customer also captured server SSE headers on the first connection:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
X-Resume-Token: rt-74f3
X-Request-Id: req-8990
```

Samir (CS): They missed the X-Resume-Token because mobile SDK dropped headers.

Priya (Billing): If we push a dedupe fix, billing team needs a clear detection rule to avoid issuing duplicate charges in the interim. Suggest: look for pairs of same customer uid + same prompt hash + completion token_count within 1m of each other -> flag for manual review and auto-credit.

Alex (Runtime): agreed. I'll scope an eng task: implement idempotency-key dedupe for generate endpoint (both streaming and non-streaming), and ensure streaming handshake includes explicit JSON metadata event at stream start { "resume_token": "...", "gen_id": "..." } so clients can persist. Also will add logs that include gen_id so CS can correlate.

reconnect-bot: incident alert attached: #billing-duplicate-spike (severity: P2) - rate 6 anomalous duplicates in last 10m.

Marta (SRE): asks: do we want server to auto-de-duplicate POSTs if they come from same session_token and prompt hash within 30s? Risk: could hide legitimate retries with changed params. We'll be conservative: return 409 + reference to existing gen_id when exact match on prompt hash + request_size + user_id + idempotency-key (if provided).

Jon (Support): Customer follow-up question: if we return 409 will the SDK surface the previous completion or an error? We should have an SDK-friendly response that includes the existing `gen_id` and a retrieval path so clients can fetch the result instead of re-creating it.

Alex (Runtime): good point. Proposed response payload on dedupe hit: 200 with body { "dedupe": true, "gen_id": "gen-5a4f", "status": "completed", "url": "/v1/generate/gen-5a4f/output" } or 409 with same body. Prefer 200 to make client UX smoother. Will propose in PR.

Priya (Billing): Timeline for credits? If eng can detect duplicates reliably, billing requests at-scale credits. If not, we should do manual credits for confirmed cases.

Alex (Runtime): I'll cut a ticket ENGR-3487, ETA 3 days for quick dedupe index + handshake metadata. Longer term: make resume_token available in SDKs and update mobile SDK to persist and reuse it.

Samir (CS): next steps for support: 1) freeze billing for this customer (assigned to Priya), 2) send customer immediate workaround (patch SDK to persist resume header + include Idempotency-Key), 3) link them to the internal ticket JIRA ENGR-3487 and let them know we're working on a server-side dedupe.

Priya (Billing): billing hold applied. Customer notified.

Marta (SRE): I'll add a dashboard panel for duplicate-generation rate and a small runbook for CS to quickly check gen_id matches across close timestamps.

Alex (Runtime): assigning to eng-runtime, tagging @marta and @samir for follow-ups. Will post PR and release notes when ready.

Jon (Support): thanks. I'll send reproduction checklist to customer: include full server logs, the mobile SDK version, the exact reconnection flow, and any X-Resume-Token headers seen.

Samir (CS): thanks team :thumbsup: — closing thread once ENGR-3487 is created and billing action completed.
